chunks: Safwan narrated from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mufrid (one performing Hajj al-Mufrid): does he hasten his Tawaf or delay it? He said, 'It is the same by Allah, whether he hastens it or delays it.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: A common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.طَوَافَهُ: Tawaf: The ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba.
key_terms.مُفْرِدِ الْحَجِّ: Mufrid: A pilgrim who performs Hajj al-Mufrid, entering the state of Ihram specifically for Hajj without combining it with Umrah.

ai.seo_question: When should a Mufrid perform their Tawaf during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility for the Mufrid regarding the timing of Tawaf al-Qudum, affirming that neither hastening nor delaying carries a specific legal disadvantage. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (yusr) in ritual acts, contrasting with schools that may emphasize immediate performance. The hadith is situated within the chapter on expiations, highlighting that while the timing is flexible, the act remains a fundamental pillar of the Hajj ritual.
